units.translation: ⟦1⟧ etc. not without a threat, cf. 711 etc. (⟦2⟧ with infinitive as at 732, Homer Il. 4.247, ⟦3⟧ 422). The question at 678 must of course be addressed to the other party, for whom Apollo answers more appropriately than Orestes; so at 679 ⟦4⟧ instead of ⟦5⟧, rightly Karsten.

⟦1⟧ = ⟦2⟧ as so often, without any relation to the ⟦3⟧ at 681, since the question is only: end or not, and the answer corresponds. Logically it should be: ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧; but so also interwoven ⟦6⟧, see there. —
so that I may be blameless in your eyes
679 ⟦1⟧, i.e. what it is not necessary to repeat. The expression is common, with various shades: ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧, etc., Wecklein on ⟦6⟧.

The surprise that this institution is only now being established, although it was already announced at 571 ff., led Kirchhoff to want to move it to after 573 (which is clearly impossible because of the conclusion at 708 ff.), and Wecklein to bracket it from beginning to end as interpolated here (while originally something similar stood after 573). If such assumptions are necessary, one will still prefer to try to come to terms with what is transmitted, and can do so quite well, cf. on 571. The court is first convened for this case, then it is to become a permanent institution; this case, then, is first submitted to it for due cognizance (573), and it now has to function and decide for the first time; at this point belongs the address to it, which only further on, as the goddess establishes it for the future, becomes an address to the whole people. For ⟦1⟧ (cf. 638) . . ⟦2⟧ 681 f. are the judges alone. After 682 Hermann (Dindorf) places verses 704-6, which is, however, inadmissible; for after them 683 f. would be quite idle. Dindorf, to be sure, declares these together with the following up to 699 to be an interpolation. One is not obliged to refute all such complicated hypotheses 1), but may regard them as refuted if what is actually transmitted proves tenable. In this, there is a close connection between 682 and 683: ⟦3⟧ –, with the same connection as already appeared twice, 483 f. and 571 ff.: immediate purpose and permanent institution. I do not think there can be any doubt about Canter's emendation ⟦4⟧ 684 for ⟦5⟧; but thus ⟦6⟧ agrees with ⟦7⟧ 682, ⟦8⟧ however with ⟦9⟧ 484 and ⟦10⟧ 572; in addition ⟦11⟧ to 570, and ⟦12⟧ to 569.
